response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same view and projection, no contrast. Differences from prior: the current image has slightly higher contrast and penetration, with crisper lung markings. Breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently, and the left chest wall device projects over a higher rib level on the current.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F6, right hilum: right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior. Indeterminate. The two reads disagreed. Not marked time-sensitive.
- F2, right lower zone: more conspicuous coarse linear markings. Indeterminate on both reads. Not marked time-sensitive.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. Coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous than on the prior (F2). This is indeterminate; both reads were indeterminate, and the higher contrast and different breast shadow position on the current may account for it. A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone on the current (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, with contour similar to the prior. Upper mediastinum not widened. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). This is indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed. The left hilum is not enlarged. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration, which may account for part of the difference.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp but is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA, with clear borders, similar to the prior.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. No soft tissue gas. Devices: left chest wall implanted venous access device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, present on both studies, with no new device (F1). The component projects over a higher rib level on the current. The central catheter course and tip are not confidently traced. Below the diaphragm: more gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen on the current, with no free gas under either dome (F5). This is indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness more conspicuous (F6), indeterminate, size change not comparable, reads disagreed. Right lower zone linear markings more conspicuous (F2), indeterminate. More left upper abdominal bowel gas (F5), indeterminate, reads disagreed. A tiny dense right lower zone focus is seen on the current but not clearly on the prior (undetermined). Technique and positional differences may account for part of these differences.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle contour and upper mediastinal width similar. Cardiac silhouette similar. Left chest wall venous access device present on both studies, with no new device (the metallic component projects at a different rib level, which may be positional).

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast. A frontal film does not separate a small nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Is the increased conspicuity of the right lower zone markings a true interval change? (F2) | Reason: The current image has higher contrast and a different breast shadow position, both of which make markings look more prominent. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the catheter tip of the left chest wall device, and has the device moved? (F1) | Reason: The central course of the tubing is not traceable through the mediastinum at this resolution. The metallic component projects at a different rib level on the two films, which soft tissue and breast positioning might explain. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing for lines. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is there a small left pleural effusion or a subtle left lower zone opacity? | Reason: Breast shadow overlaps the left costophrenic region and lower zone on both films, and there is no lateral view. | Recommend: Lateral view if clinically relevant.
- Are there subtle lesions in the ribs or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail such as pedicles and small lucent lesions is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.
- Is the right hilar and infrahilar fullness a real interval change, such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass, or prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique? (F6) | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration than the prior. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast. A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available.
- Is the small dense nodular focus over the medial right lower zone on the current a true lung nodule, a calcified granuloma, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: It is a small focus on X-ray within crowded bronchovascular markings and breast shadow, and no definite matching focus is seen at the same site on the softer prior image. | Recommend: CT chest.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone linear markings a true interstitial change? (F2) | Reason: The current is sharper and slightly different in exposure and inspiration, and breast shadow overlies the region on both films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If the difference persists there, CT chest.
- Where is the port catheter tip, and has the port or catheter moved? (F1) | Reason: The catheter tip cannot be traced over the mediastinum at this image resolution. The different projected level of the reservoir may reflect arm and breast position only. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing to trace the catheter to its tip. Add a lateral view if tip position remains unclear.
- Is the heterogeneous texture of the left humeral head a bone lesion or a normal or degenerative appearance? | Reason: The images are low resolution and the shoulder is at the edge of a chest film, so fine bone detail is unreliable. The appearance is similar on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the appearance persists.

IMPRESSION:
1. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). Indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed. Technique differences may account for part of this. Triage: high urgency, radiologist review next shift, no on-call page.
2. More conspicuous coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone (F2). Indeterminate on both reads. Technique and breast shadow position may account for this.
3. Tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current. Undetermined whether a nodule or a vessel end-on.
4. No definite lung mass, confluent opacity, right pleural effusion or destructive rib lesion on the current PA. Upper mediastinum not widened. The left costophrenic region is partly hidden by breast shadow.
5. Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, with no new device. Catheter tip not traced, and a position change cannot be judged.
6. More left upper abdominal bowel gas on the current (F5). Indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed. No free gas under either dome.
7. Left humeral head texture undetermined. Aortic knuckle prominence and cardiac silhouette are similar to the prior.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the right hilar fullness (F6) and the tiny right lower zone focus. The interval is not specified in the findings and is left to the attending.
- Review the source images in PACS, including bone windows and line windowing, before the CT decision.
- Short-interval repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph, or CT chest, if there is clinical concern about the right lower zone markings (F2).
- Lateral view if left lower zone or pleural assessment, or catheter tip position, matters clinically.
- Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the left humeral head appearance persists on source review.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
